paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David says, "I was glad when they said to me, 'Let us go to the house of the LORD.'" (Psalm 122:1) Glad! Not dragging his feet, not checking his phone for an excuse. This song is about what it looks like when a heart loves being near God and near God's people.

And watch where that gladness leads him. The tribes go up together "to give thanks to the name of the LORD." (Psalm 122:4) Then David turns around and asks for something: "Pray for the peace of Jerusalem." (Psalm 122:6) He loves the place God's people gather, so he prays for it, speaks peace over it, and seeks its good.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Gathering with God's people is a gift to be glad about, and praying for their peace is part of loving them. David says he does it "For the sake of my brothers and friends" and "For the sake of the house of the LORD our God." (Psalm 122:8-9) Next time somebody says, "Let's go," let your FACE answer first, baker, and then go bring some peace with you.
